name: Ra I experimental papyrus vessel
summary: Ra was a papyrus-reed boat built at Giza in 1969 for an experimental Atlantic voyage from Morocco; damaged, it was left at sea before reaching Barbados.
description: The specific 1969 Ra papyrus-reed vessel used by Thor Heyerdahl’s expedition, distinct from the later Ra II.
tier_reason: Fine detail: a specific short-lived experimental papyrus vessel and voyage.
why: Thor Heyerdahl wanted to show that boats of the kind pictured in ancient Egypt could have crossed the Atlantic, so he had one built and sailed from Morocco.

market.note: The sources describe one custom-built expedition vessel deployed for a research voyage, and the expedition leader described the voyage as a scientific experiment. The classification applies to that use and does not deny sponsorship, paid builders, media rights or possible transactions.

date.basis: The museum dates construction of this vessel to 1969.

events.statement: The papyrus vessel Ra was built in 1969 for the expedition.
events.caveats: Construction month and day are not specified; this is not a claim about the invention of reed boats. The museum page has conflicting Giza prose and a Safi caption; the contemporary Salén-Nytt account independently corroborates Giza.

events.statement: Ra departed Safi on the expedition’s experimental Atlantic voyage.
events.caveats: A voyage beginning is not evidence of historical pre-Columbian contact and does not imply the crossing succeeded.

date.label: 16–22 July 1969
date.basis: A contemporary Reuters report puts initial evacuation on Wednesday 16 July while a return was contemplated; by the 22 July datelined interview Ra was reported left behind.

events.statement: The crew left the damaged Ra at sea and reached Barbados aboard Shenandoah; the 1969 voyage in Ra was abandoned.
events.caveats: First departure and final decision may not be the same moment. The contemporaneous interview says the later fate of Ra was then unknown; this event applies only to Ra and that voyage.

earliest_record.rationale: The actual 25 May departure documents deployment of this particular vessel, distinct from construction. The expedition subsequently abandoned Ra I; the separate abandonment event remains. This experiment does not establish ancient transatlantic contact.

caveats: The expedition tests a particular modern voyage; it cannot establish prehistoric transatlantic contact. Ra II was a new vessel; no abandonment of the reed-boat family is claimed.

unresolved.note: The 1969 vessel was constructed for the voyage, but the first invention of reed vessels is not established.
